6:10.headline: Flinching like a hand from boiling water
6:10.body: ואסלדה appears only here, so Rashi and Ramban turn to the sages' Hebrew, where a hand סולדת, "flinches", from scalding water. Rav Hai Gaon, cited by Ibn Ezra, reads it as "lifting up".

sources.quote: וַאֲנִי אֵינִי מוֹצֵא לוֹ דִּמְיוֹן בַּמִּקְרָא, זוּלָתִי שֶׁבִּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה
sources.says: Rashi says he finds no parallel in Scripture, only in the language of the Mishnah.

sources.quote: שֶׁהַיָּד סוֹלֶדֶת בָּהֶן מִלִּכָּווֹת בָּרוֹתְחִין
sources.says: Rashi cites the phrase about a hand flinching from being scalded.

sources.quote: ולשון ואסלדה, אין לו דומה במקרא, אבל בלשון חכמים הנכוה ומכויץ עצמו נקרא כן
sources.says: Ramban says the word has no parallel in Scripture, but the sages use it for one who is burned and shrinks back.

sources.quote: ואני ראיתי רב האיי ז"ל שפירש: ואסלדה, לשון הגבהה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that Rav Hai Gaon explained ואסלדה as lifting up.

6:14.headline: Kindness, or disgrace
6:14.body: חסד usually means kindness, and Rashi reads the friend who withholds kindness. Metzudat Zion and Ralbag read the rarer sense "disgrace", as in Leviticus 20:17: the sufferer gets shame from his friends.

sources.quote: לְמִי שֶׁמּוֹנֵעַ חֶסֶד מֵחֲבֵירוֹ
sources.says: Rashi reads it as one who holds back kindness from his friend.

sources.quote: חסד. ענינו חרפה כמו חסד הוא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חסד here means disgrace, as in Leviticus 20:17.

sources.quote: היתכן שלאיש המס אשר המסו אותו רוב הצרות הבאות עליו יהי' מרעהו חרפ'
sources.says: Ralbag asks whether a man worn down by troubles should get disgrace from his friend.

6:17.headline: Scorched by the sun, or running off like a gutter
6:17.body: יזרבו appears only here. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as יצרבו, "scorched", swapping ז for צ, while Ramban reads it from מרזב, "gutter": streams that run in the rain and vanish in the heat.

sources.quote: בְּעֵת יְזֹרְבוּ. לְשׁוֹן יְצֹרְבוּ, כְּחוֹם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says יזרבו means scorched, as by the sun's heat.

sources.quote: יזורבו. כמו יצרבו כי זסשר״ץ מתחלפים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it stands for יצרבו, since these letters can swap.

sources.quote: בעת יזרבו, הפך מן מרזב, בעת יזובו מי הגשמים
sources.says: Ramban says it comes from מרזב, a gutter, for when rainwater flows.

sources.quote: ויהיה ענין יזורבו יתחממו ואין לו חבר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means they grow hot and has no partner in the Bible.

6:21.headline: You have become nothing, or become like that stream
6:21.body: The verse is written לא, "not", and the Targum reads "you have become as nothing". Rashi and Ibn Ezra read לו: Rashi says the friends are like the failing stream, and Ibn Ezra says they sided with God out of fear.

sources.quote: אֲרוּם כְּדוּן הֲוֵיתוּן כְּלָא
sources.says: The Targum says: for now you have become as nothing.

sources.quote: כִּי עַתָּה הֱיִיתֶם לוֹ. הֱיִיתֶם נִמְשָׁלִים לְאוֹתוֹ נַחַל
sources.says: Rashi reads לו and says the friends have become like that stream.

sources.quote: כי עתה הייתם לו - למקום כאשר ראיתם החתת שהביא עלי ותיראו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reads לו as "to God": the friends sided with Him when they saw the ruin He brought and grew afraid.

6:25.headline: How strong, or how eloquent, honest words are
6:25.body: Ibn Ezra reads נמרצו as "strong", like the "grievous curse" of I Kings 2:8. Rashi swaps ר for ל to hear נמלצו, "well spoken", as in "how sweet (נמלצו) to my palate" in Psalms.

sources.quote: נמרצו - חזקו כמו: קללה נמרצת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says נמרצו means they are strong, as in "a grievous curse".

sources.quote: וְכֵן ״נִמְלְצוּ לְחִכִּי״ (תהלים קיט:קג) – כֻּלָּן לְשׁוֹן מְלִיצָה הֵם, וְלָמֶ״ד מִתְחַלֶּפֶת בְּרֵי״שׁ
sources.says: Rashi links it to נמלצו in Psalms 119:103 and says these all mean fine speech, with ל and ר swapping.

6:26.headline: Empty words, or the words of a man without hope
6:26.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read נאש as "worthless", as in Jeremiah 2:25. Ralbag reads it as Job naming himself "the one who has given up hope".

sources.quote: אִמְרֵי נוֹאָשׁ. שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם מַמָּשׁ, כְּמוֹ ״וַתֹּאמְרִי נוֹאָשׁ״
sources.says: Rashi says these are words with nothing in them, as in Jeremiah 2:25.

sources.quote: נואש. ענין דבר שאין בו ממש ואין לחשוש עליו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נואש means something empty that need not be heeded.

sources.quote: אמרי נואש. קרא עצמו נואש להיותו נואש מטוב
sources.says: Ralbag says Job calls himself נואש because he has given up hope of good.

7:1.headline: A soldier's service, or a fixed stretch of time
7:1.body: צבא usually means an army. Metzudat Zion reads it here as a fixed span of time, and Malbim explains why: a lifetime is moments gathered together, like soldiers gathered into an army.

sources.quote: צבא. קץ וזמן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says צבא here means an end point and a set time.

sources.quote: צבא. בא גם על הזמן
sources.says: Malbim says צבא also means time, because a span of time gathers moments the way an army gathers men.

sources.quote: הֲלָא חֵילָא לְבַר נָשׁ
sources.says: The Targum keeps the army sense: "is there not a force for man".

7:3.headline: Months of misery: a midrash counts a full year
7:3.body: Job speaks of "months of emptiness". A midrash takes the months as a count, one year, and says Job suffered during the twelve months God's hand was on Egypt.

sources.quote: וכל אותו הזמן איוב נידון ביסורין, שנאמר כן הנחלתי לי ירחי שוא
sources.says: The midrash says Job was judged with suffering through the twelve months of Egypt's plagues, citing this verse.

sources.quote: ירחים של מנין זו שנה
sources.says: It reads "months that are counted" as one year.

7:4.headline: Measuring the long night, or the night slipping away
7:4.body: ומדד appears only here. Ibn Ezra reads it from מדד, "measure": Job measures out the long evening. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it from נדד, "wander off", as when Jacob's sleep fled from his eyes.

sources.quote: ומדד ערב - מן וימדדם בחבל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from measuring, as with a measuring line.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן ״וַתִּדַּד שְׁנָתִי״
sources.says: Rashi says it comes from "my sleep fled", with the מ as a prefix.

sources.quote: ומדד. מל׳ נדידה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from wandering.

7:5.headline: A clod of earth, written one way and read another
7:5.body: The word is read גוש, "clod", but written גיש. Ibn Ezra lists three guesses for it and picks "clod of earth", and a midrash on odd letters says its ג is written small, a hint at the grave.

sources.quote: ואחרים אמרו: שהוא מין חיות. והקרוב שהוא מין עפר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some tie it to groping, others to a kind of animal, and he thinks it is a kind of earth.

sources.ref: Otzar Midrashim, Midrashim of Rabbi Akiba, The Small Letters and their Purposes 5
sources.quote: הקרי וגוש בוי״ו אבל הכתיב וגיש ביו״ד
sources.says: The midrash says the word is read with ו but written with י, that its ג is small, and links this to the three days after death.

sources.quote: גּוּשַׁת עָפָר, וְהִיא הֶעֶלְתָה חֲלוּדָּה
sources.says: Rashi says it is a clod of earth that grows damp and mold.

7:5.headline: Job's skin is loathsome, or it melts away
7:5.body: וימאס usually means "and it was rejected". Metzudat Zion and Ramban read it as מסס, "melt", with an א standing in, while Ibn Ezra keeps the plain sense: the skin had become repulsive.

sources.quote: וימאס. מל׳ המסה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from melting.

sources.quote: ויש מפרשים וימאס כמו וימסס
sources.says: Ramban says some read it as "melted", and the Targum agrees.

sources.quote: ויהיה וימאס כמשמעו, בעבור שנשתנה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports the "melt" reading but keeps the plain meaning, because the skin changed.

7:6.headline: Days end without hope, or when the thread runs out
7:6.body: תקוה means hope, but also a cord, as in Rahab's scarlet thread. Right after the weaver's shuttle, Ibn Ezra and Ramban note it can mean the days end when the thread runs out.

sources.quote: באפס תקוה - בהכרת תקות החוט, או תקוה ממש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means when the thread is cut off, or simply hope.

sources.quote: ואחרים פירשו מן תקות שני
sources.says: Ramban reads "without hope", and says others read it from Rahab's scarlet cord.

7:8.headline: The word for seeing hidden in the word for a gift
7:8.body: תשורני means "will see me". A midrash asks why a gift is called תשורה, and answers from this verse: because people gaze at it and say how lovely it is.

sources.quote: למה נקרא דורון תשורה. דבר נש מסתכל בה
sources.says: Rabbi Simon says a gift is called תשורה because people look at it, citing this verse.

sources.quote: תשורני. תראני
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means "will see me".

7:18.headline: Every morning: the Talmud learns people are judged daily
7:18.body: Job complains that God checks on him every morning and tests him every moment. In the Talmud, Rabbi Yosi learns from "every morning" that a person is judged every day, and Rabbi Natan learns from "every moment" that it is every hour.

sources.quote: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אָדָם נִידּוֹן בְּכׇל יוֹם
sources.says: Rabbi Yosi says a person is judged every day, citing this verse.

sources.quote: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: אָדָם נִידּוֹן בְּכׇל שָׁעָה
sources.says: Rabbi Natan says a person is judged every hour, from "every moment".

sources.quote: לבקרים - לכל בקר וענינו תמיד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means every morning, that is, always.

8:4.headline: Sent off by their sin, or struck down where they sinned
8:4.body: ביד usually means "by the hand of", and Rashi reads it that way: their sin itself became the messenger that took them. The Targum and Metzudat Zion read יד as a place, so Job's children died right where they sinned, at the feast.

sources.quote: (הַפֶּשַׁע) הוּא נַעֲשָׂה שָׁלִיחַ לְהוֹבִילָם
sources.says: Rashi says the sin became the messenger that carried them off.

sources.quote: והתרגום אמר: באתר מרדיהון, כמו יד הירדן
sources.says: Ramban notes the Targum reads it as "in the place of their rebellion", as יד means a place by the Jordan.

sources.quote: ביד. במקום כמו יד אבשלום
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ביד means "in the place", as in "Absalom's monument".

sources.quote: כי בבית המשתה מתו במקום הרשע שם המשפט
sources.says: Metzudat David says they died in the house of feasting, the place of their wrongdoing.

8:6.headline: "If you are pure", not "if you were"
8:6.body: Bildad says "if you are pure and upright". A midrash notices he did not say "if you were": the wording hints that in the past he was not yet righteous.

sources.quote: הָיִיתָ אֵין כְּתִיב כָּאן אֶלָּא אָתָּה, הָא לְשֶׁעָבַר לֹא הָיָה צַדִּיק
sources.says: The midrash says the verse writes "you are", not "you were", so in the past he was not righteous.

8:6.headline: The home of your righteousness: your house, or your soul
8:6.body: נוה means a dwelling. Ramban reads it as Job's home, which God will fill again with children and wealth, while Ibn Ezra and Ralbag read it as his soul, where righteousness lives.

sources.quote: כי ישלם בנים ועושר ונכסים בנוה הצדק שיהיה לך
sources.says: Ramban says God will restore children, wealth and property to Job's righteous home.

sources.quote: ושלם נות צדקך - היא הנשמה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the dwelling of righteousness is the soul.

sources.quote: נות צדקך. ר"ל נפשך כי הנפש היא נות הצדק ומשכנו
sources.says: Ralbag says it means your soul, since the soul is where righteousness lives.

8:11.headline: The reed named for gulping water
8:11.body: גמא is a reed that grows only in wet marsh. A midrash says it is called גמא because it gulps (גומא) water all the time, the word Eliezer uses when he asks Rebecca, "let me sip a little water" (Genesis 24:17).

sources.quote: למה נקרא גומא, שהוא גומא ושותה מיא תדיר ודומה לדבר הגמיאני נא מעט מים
sources.says: The midrash says the reed is called גומא because it always gulps and drinks water, like "let me sip a little water".

sources.quote: אֵין הַגֹּמֶא גָּדֵל אֶלָּא בְּעוֹד שֶׁהַבִּצָּה לַחָה בְּמֵימֶיהָ
sources.says: Rashi says the reed grows only while the marsh is wet.

8:11.headline: A reed without water, Israel without Torah
8:11.body: Bildad asks if a reed can grow without water. The sages read it as Israel without Torah: when they let go of it, Amalek attacked.

sources.quote: כָּךְ אֵי אֶפְשָׁר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מִתְעַסְּקִין בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
sources.says: The Mekhilta says that just as the reed cannot grow without water, Israel cannot live unless they are busy with Torah.

sources.quote: וּלְפִי שֶׁפֵּרְשׁוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה, לְפִיכָךְ הַשּׂוֹנֵא בָּא עֲלֵיהֶם
sources.says: The midrash says that because Israel left off the words of Torah, the enemy came against them.

8:13.headline: The flatterer who flatters his own desires
8:13.body: Metzudat Zion says the wicked man is called חנף, a flatterer, because he flatters his own desires and gives in to them. The Targum renders it דילטור, an informer.

sources.quote: חנף. כן יקרא הרשע על כי מחניף ליצרו וממלא פתוייו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the wicked man is called this because he flatters his urges and does what they entice him to do.

sources.quote: וּסְבַר מִדִילָטוֹר תְּהוֹבַד
sources.says: The Targum renders it "the hope of the informer will be lost".

8:14.headline: His trust is cut down, or shrinks to almost nothing
8:14.body: This word appears only here. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as cutting off, while Malbim also offers "grows small", from כמעט קט, "just a little".

sources.quote: יָקוֹט, לְשׁוֹן קָצִיר, כְּמוֹ (יחזקאל טז:מז) ״כִּמְעַט קָט״
sources.says: Rashi says it means cutting, as in a harvest.

sources.quote: יקוט. יוכרת כמו ונקטו בפניהם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means "will be cut off".

sources.quote: יקוט, פי' מענין כריתה. ויל"פ מענין כמעט קט, שכסלו נעשה קטן וחלוש
sources.says: Malbim says it means cutting, or that his trust becomes small and weak.

sources.quote: פי' הגאון בו: (הבל)[חבל] השמש, והוא רחוק, לכן הוא מן ונקוטותם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports the Gaon's reading, calls it far-fetched, and ties the word to ונקוטותם in Ezekiel.

8:14.headline: Trust spun from his own body, like a spider's web
8:14.body: Malbim says a spider's web is woven from threads out of the spider's own body. So the wicked man's trust has no root outside his own imagination, and Rashi adds that, like a web, it does not last.

sources.quote: שהוא ארוג מחוטים היוצאים מגוף העכביש, כן מבטחו אין לו שורש רק בעצם דמיונו
sources.says: Malbim says the web is woven from threads from the spider's body, and the wicked man's trust is rooted only in his imagination.

sources.quote: וּבֵית עַכָּבִישׁ. שֶׁאֵינוֹ קַיָּם
sources.says: Rashi says the spider's house does not last.

8:17.headline: Roots by a spring, or wrapped around a heap of stones
8:17.body: גל can mean a spring or a heap. Metzudat Zion and Ralbag read it as a spring of water feeding the roots, while Ibn Ezra and Ramban read it as a heap of stones the roots wind around.

sources.quote: גל. מעין כמו גולת מים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a spring.

sources.quote: שעל גל המים יסתבכו שרשיו
sources.says: Ralbag says the roots tangle at the spring of water.

sources.quote: על גל - כמו: גל אבנים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means a heap of stones.

sources.quote: שרשיו יסובכו, על גל אבנים אשר ימצאו בהשתרשם
sources.says: Ramban says the roots wind around a heap of stones they meet as they spread.

8:19.headline: Others grow in his place, or he regrows in new soil
8:19.body: Rashi reads אחר as another person, who will rise to take the wicked man's place. Metzudat David and Malbim read it as other soil: the uprooted tree is replanted and grows better, as the righteous do after suffering.

sources.quote: אָדָם אַחֵר יִצְמַח לְקַבֵּל גְּדֻלָּתוֹ שֶׁל זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says another person will grow up to receive this man's greatness.

sources.quote: כי מעפר אחר אשר עתה ינטע בו יצמחו לו יונקות באופן יותר שלם
sources.says: Metzudat David says the tree, planted in other soil, will put out better shoots.

sources.quote: כי מעפר אחר אשר אין שם אבנים ושרשים משם יצמחו שרשיו באין מעכב
sources.says: Malbim says that in other soil, free of stones, its roots will grow without anything in the way.

9:5.headline: The sages hear Sodom in mountains that shook and were overturned
9:5.body: Rashi compares this overturning to Sodom's. The midrash says that for 25 years God shook the mountains around Sodom so its people would repent. They did not notice, so He overturned them.

sources.quote: הַמְּסַלְּקָם, כְּהָפְכוֹ סְדוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says God removes them as when He overturned Sodom.

sources.quote: עֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנָה הָיָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַרְעִישׁ עֲלֵיהֶם הָרִים וּמֵבִיא עֲלֵיהֶם זְוָעוֹת כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּעֲשׂוּ תְּשׁוּבָה, וְלֹא עָשׂוּ
sources.says: The midrash says for 25 years God shook mountains and sent tremors on Sodom so they would repent, and they did not.

9:8.headline: "By Himself": no angel helped stretch the sky
9:8.body: Rashi stops on לבדו, "alone". Angels were made only on the second day, he says. So no one can claim the angel Michael stretched out the north and Gabriel the south.

sources.quote: וּמַלְאָכִים נִבְרְאוּ בַּיּוֹם שֵׁנִי, שֶׁלֹּא תֹּאמַר: מִיכָאֵל מָתַח בַּצָּפוֹן, וְגַבְרִיאֵל בַּדָּרוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says angels were created on the second day, so one cannot say Michael stretched the north and Gabriel the south.

9:9.headline: Which stars are עש? The Talmud gives two answers
9:9.body: עש names a group of stars and appears only twice. The Talmud calls it יותא and says it is either the tail of the Ram or the head of the Calf. Ibn Ezra says it is seven stars.

sources.quote: מַאי ״עָשׁ״? אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: יוֹתָא. מַאי ״יוֹתָא״? אָמְרִי לַהּ זְנַב טָלֶה. וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רֵישָׁא דְעִגְלָא
sources.says: The Talmud says עש is יותא, which some say is the tail of the Ram and others the head of the Calf.

sources.quote: עש - הם שבעה כוכבים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says עש is seven stars.

9:9.headline: One star group brings cold, the other heat, and each saves the world
9:9.body: Here the verse lists כסיל before כימה, and Amos 5:8 has the reverse. Shmuel explains: the heat of כסיל and the cold of כימה each hold the other back. Without both, the world could not last.

sources.quote: אִלְמָלֵא חַמָּה שֶׁל כְּסִיל, לֹא נִתְקַיֵּים עוֹלָם מִפְּנֵי צִינָּה שֶׁל כִּימָה
sources.says: Shmuel says that without the heat of כסיל the world could not survive the cold of כימה, and the reverse.

9:13.headline: רהב: arrogance, or a name for Egypt?
9:13.body: רהב means pride. Rashi reads it as a name for Egypt, as in Isaiah 30:7, given for its arrogance. Then the verse speaks of the heavenly forces that came to help Egypt and had to bow.

sources.quote: מִצְרַיִם נִקְרָא רַהַב, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״לָכֵן קָרָאתִי לָזֹאת רַהַב הֵם שָׁבֶת״
sources.says: Rashi says Egypt is called רהב, as in Isaiah 30:7.

sources.quote: רהב. ענין גאוה והתחזקות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says רהב means pride and self-assertion.

9:23.headline: A whip, a sudden flood, or the Satan?
9:23.body: שוט usually means a whip, and Metzudat Zion keeps that. Rashi reads it as a word for the Satan. Maimonides reads it as a sudden flood that sweeps away everyone in its path.

sources.quote: שוט. שרביט כמו שוט לסוס
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says שוט is a rod, like a whip for a horse.

sources.quote: אִם שׁוֹט. לָשׁוֹן שֶׁל שָׂטָן
sources.says: Rashi says שוט is a word for the Satan.

sources.quote: כלומר: אם שיטפון בא לפתע וממית וסוחף את כל מי שהוא פוגש בו
sources.says: Maimonides explains it as a flood that comes suddenly and kills and sweeps away everyone it meets.

9:23.headline: Mocking the innocent as they melt, or as they are tested?
9:23.body: מסה appears only here. Metzudat Zion and the Targum read it as melting: the innocent waste away. Ralbag reads it as testing, from נסה: the wicked mock how God tests the innocent.

sources.quote: למסת. מלשון המסה והמגה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from melting.

sources.quote: כַּד מִתְמַסְמְסִין זַכָּאִין יִדְחָךְ
sources.says: The Targum translates: when the innocent melt away, He laughs.

sources.quote: ילעג לראות אשר ינסה בהם השם יתברך הנקיים
sources.says: Ralbag says the wicked mock to see how God tests the innocent.

9:24.headline: The wicked one who runs the earth: God, or the Satan?
9:24.body: Rabbi Eliezer says Job meant God here, and so tried to turn the bowl upside down, overturning everything. Rabbi Yehoshua says Job spoke only of the Satan. Rashi follows Rabbi Yehoshua.

sources.quote: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: בִּקֵּשׁ אִיּוֹב לַהֲפוֹךְ קְעָרָה עַל פִּיהָ. אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: לֹא דִּבֵּר אִיּוֹב אֶלָּא כְּלַפֵּי שָׂטָן
sources.says: Rabbi Eliezer says Job tried to turn the bowl upside down, and Rabbi Yehoshua says Job spoke only about the Satan.

sources.quote: בְּיַד רָשָׁע. כְּלַפֵּי שָׂטָן
sources.says: Rashi says the wicked one is the Satan.

9:26.headline: Ships of אבה: a river, a wish, or enemies?
9:26.body: אבה appears only here. Rashi says it is the name of a fast river. Ralbag reads "desire": ships that reach where they want. Ramban notes the Targum reads איבה, enmity: enemy ships rushing to plunder.

sources.quote: אֵבֶה. שֵׁם נָהָר שׁוֹטֵף
sources.says: Rashi says אבה is the name of a rushing river.

sources.quote: אניות אבה. הוא מעניין רצון
sources.says: Ralbag says אבה comes from wanting.

sources.quote: אמר התרגום ספינן קלילן דמרי דבבו דאזלין למיבז, מל' איבה
sources.says: Ramban says the Targum reads it as swift ships of enemies going to plunder, from איבה.

9:26.headline: A word with no partner in Scripture, read from Aramaic
9:26.body: Ibn Ezra says יטוש has no other example in the Bible, so he reads "flies" from context. Ramban hears the Aramaic טאיס, to fly, as in the Targum and the sages' phrase for flying through the air.

sources.quote: יטוש - אין לו ריע במקרא ופירושו: יעוף, לפי העניין
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says יטוש has no partner in Scripture and means flies, from context.

sources.quote: כנשרא דטאיס למיכל, ובלשון הגדה, טיסין באוירא
sources.says: Ramban cites the Aramaic "like an eagle that flies to eat" and the aggadic phrase "flying in the air".

9:28.headline: I fear all my pains, or I have gathered them all?
9:28.body: יגרתי usually means "I feared", and Ramban reads it so. Metzudat Zion and the Targum read it as "I gathered", like אוגר, storing up in summer (Proverbs 10:5): Job has piled up all his pains.

sources.quote: יגורתי, כי גם כן יבואו כל עצבותי
sources.says: Ramban says Job fears that all his pains will come.

sources.quote: יגורתי. אאסוף כמו אוגר בקיץ
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says יגורתי means I gather, as in Proverbs 10:5.

sources.quote: כְּנַשֵׁית כּוּלְהוֹן צַעֲרִי
sources.says: The Targum translates: I gathered all my pains.

9:32.headline: משפט covers the whole case: argument, verdict, punishment
9:32.body: Rashi says משפט has three senses, one for each stage of a case: the arguing, the verdict, and the punishment or collecting the debt. Scripture can mean any of them. Here it means the arguing.

sources.quote: מִשְׁפָּט מְשַׁמֵּשׁ שָׁלֹשׁ לְשׁוֹנוֹת: תְּחִלָּתוֹ הוֹכָחַת דְּבָרִים, אֶמְצָעִיתוֹ פְּסַק דִּין, וְסוֹפוֹ מִשְׁטַר יִסּוּרִין וְגִבּוּי חוֹב
sources.says: Rashi says משפט has three senses: first arguing, then the verdict, and finally punishment and collecting the debt.

sources.quote: בַּמִּשְׁפָּט. בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹכָחוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says that here it means words of argument.

9:33.headline: Job wants an umpire between himself and God
9:33.body: Rashi explains מוכיח as an arbiter who shows each side its guilt and its merit. Rav in the Talmud is sharp about Job's wish: "Dust in Job's mouth! Can a servant argue with his master?"

sources.quote: מַרְאֶה לְכָל אֶחָד חוֹבָתוֹ וּזְכוּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the מוכיח shows each side its guilt and its merit.

sources.quote: אָמַר רַב: עַפְרָא לְפוּמֵּיהּ דְּאִיּוֹב, כְּלוּם יֵשׁ עֶבֶד שֶׁמּוֹכִיחַ אֶת רַבּוֹ
sources.says: Rav says dust in Job's mouth, for no servant argues against his master.

9:34.headline: A scribal tradition writes this ט in an odd size
9:34.body: Old lists of unusual letters mark the ט of שבטו, "His rod". One list says it is small, another says it is large. Both give the same reason: no suffering was like Job's.

sources.ref: Otzar Midrashim, Midrashim of Rabbi Akiba, The Small Letters and their Purposes 18
sources.quote: יסר מעלי שבטו (איוב ט' ל״ד) ט' קטנה, כי לא יסורין כיסורין של איוב
sources.says: This list says the ט is small, because no suffering is like Job's.

sources.ref: Otzar Midrashim, Midrashim of Rabbi Akiba, The Enlarged Letters 11
sources.quote: וכן יסר מעלי שבטו (איוב ט׳ ל״ד) שלא היתה כמכת איוב
sources.says: This list counts the ט as large, because there was no blow like Job's.
